title: Website Security Order Desk Rule: One Plan per Site Domain
content:
**Rule.** A customer may protect any number of sites with Website Security, one plan per site. A new Harborline SiteGuard plan may be ordered for a site domain only when no other plan for that site domain is in status pending setup, active, cancel pending or expired.

## What the rule turns on

- **Number of sites.** No limit is set on the number of sites, and so on the number of plans, a customer may hold; the limit is one plan per site domain.
- **The site domain.** Each plan records the domain of the protected site in lowercase, exactly as given. The test compares the site domain of the new order with the site domain recorded on the company's existing plans.
- **Evidence.** The test is decided from the company's plan records as they stand before the order is placed, not from the customer's account of which sites are already protected.

## Status of an existing plan for the same site domain

| Existing plan's status | Does it prevent a new order for that site domain under this rule? |
|---|---|
| Pending setup | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| Cancel pending | Yes |
| Expired | Yes |
| Cancelled | No |

A cancelled plan is not among the four statuses listed, so it does not prevent a new order for its site domain under this rule.

## Illustrations (hypothetical domains)

1. A customer holds an active plan for northpier-example.test and orders a plan for quayside-example.test. The two site domains differ, so the existing plan does not prevent the new order.
2. A customer's plan for northpier-example.test expired and has not been cancelled. A new plan for northpier-example.test may not be ordered while that plan's status is expired.
3. The same customer's plan for northpier-example.test later ends and its status is cancelled. That plan no longer prevents a new order for northpier-example.test.
